items.title: Joe Lyde Interview, 1959-05-18
items.q: He said that, uh, Ravel and Tabusi were Bix's favorite, uh, composers and he was stashing up every Ravel and Tabusi disc he could lay his hands on.

ctx.x: Nothing dirty? Did they play any dirty type music?

No, no, more smooth. He liked to croon and that a little, you know, but it was like those Muggsy records. And then the trombone player was very like, I'm reminded of a parallel, it was very like the way The Last Straws is going now. This band I've been playing in, uh, they've been publicized as a society band and they've certainly got all their jobs as a society band through contacts rather than ability, I would say. I would suggest I don't, uh... And gradually the peasants are taking over. You see, the sort of…
You gotta have some kind of, you gotta have some kind of.
